item.title: formal-lib
item.description:
Software verifiers all report the same kinds of facts and every one of them says it differently. Anything built on top of a verifier starts by writing a parser, and that parser has to be tested, maintained, and rewritten when the tool’s output drifts. Add a second verifier and you do it again, into a second shape that doesn’t line up with the first.

formal-lib does that work once. Verifier output goes in, a stable structured model comes out: issues with severity and error type, stack traces, and counterexample traces with variable assignments.

item.title: Entoli
item.description:
Entoli (εντολή) is the Greek word for a command, both the one you give and the one the agent runs.

Entoli is a general-purpose open-source assistant designed to give you full-control. It uses Byte Repair technologies to securely check the code it generates in order to ensure it is safe and can be trusted. In the age of agentic-coding, LLMs can create code that has vulnerabilities (i.e. memory leaks, overflow/underflow, array bounds access failures, etc.). Byte Repair is designed to find these vulnerabilities and automatically fix them. Byte Repair automatically encodes the program as a mathematically constrained equation to find vulnerabilities.

item.title: Byte Repair Enterprise Server
item.description:
The Enterprise Server is the full method running continuously against a team’s repositories, rather than a tool a developer invokes by hand.

Runs On Your Servers, By Design

The Enterprise Server is installed on your own infrastructure and stays there. This is a compliance decision before it is a technical one: for the codebases this is built for: safety-critical, regulated, or simply contractually fenced. Code that leaves the building is a problem no feature list can answer.

item.title: Verifying ESBMC With Itself
item.description: Byte Repair is the first tool to formally verify the ESBMC Operational Model; work that will improve ESBMC’s accuracy and reduce false results from edge cases.
